\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Invariance}

\section{Overview}
Fourth-order invariance compares independent input laws through squared influences, with variance-normalized smooth and Lipschitz consequences.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-order invariance principle]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.basic_invariance_principle}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments.identDistrib, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.identDistrib_of_independent_coordinates, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_of_independent_pair, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$; let $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$. Let $X=(X_i)$ and $Y=(Y_i)$ be families of independent real inputs on probability spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, respectively. Each input is measurable up to a null set, has finite fourth absolute moment, and has first, second, and third moments $0,1,0$ and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $C^4$ and $C\ge0$ satisfies $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t$, then $|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E_\nu\psi(F(Y))|\le (C/12)9^k\sum_i I_i(F)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Smooth invariance under small influences]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_small_influences}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.basic_invariance_principle, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_sq_influences_le_degree_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.has_degree_at_most_eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$; let $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$. Let $X=(X_i)$ and $Y=(Y_i)$ be families of independent real inputs on probability spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, respectively. Each input is measurable up to a null set, has finite fourth absolute moment, and has first, second, and third moments $0,1,0$ and fourth moment at most $9$. Suppose $\sum_{S\ne\varnothing}a_S^2\le1$, $\varepsilon\ge0$, and $I_i(F)\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, then $|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E_\nu\psi(F(Y))|\le (C/12)k9^k\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential bound on the degree factor]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.degree_mul_nine_pow_le_sixteen_pow}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $k\ge0$, the real-number inequality $k9^k\le16^k$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth root of the invariance scale]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_quarter_power_le}
\leanok

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Universal Lipschitz invariance estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_lipschitz}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_expectation_bound_of_fourth_derivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_quarter_power_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_small_influences, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}

There exists a universal real constant $K>0$ with the following property. Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$; let $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$. Let $X=(X_i)$ and $Y=(Y_i)$ be families of independent real inputs on probability spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, respectively. Each input is measurable up to a null set, has finite fourth absolute moment, and has first, second, and third moments $0,1,0$ and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\sum_{S\ne\varnothing}a_S^2\le1$, $\varepsilon\ge0$, $I_i(F)\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$, and $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $c$-Lipschitz with $c\ge0$, then $|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E_\nu\psi(F(Y))|\le Kc2^k\varepsilon^{1/4}$.
\end{theorem}
